feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV for a senior digital communications role: clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant technical breadth. It reads polished and substantive, but impact would improve with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative: the summary aligns well with the work history and shows steady advancement into leadership.  
- Strong credibility: NACo progression is compelling, and the mix of strategy, operations, web, analytics, and multimedia is well evidenced.  
- Good specificity: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, studio buildout, and website migration details make the profile concrete and marketable.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include metrics like email growth, engagement lifts, traffic gains, production volume, cost savings, or team size managed.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would tighten structure and improve scanability.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; keep comma usage consistent in lists (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings or typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it reads a bit generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and anchoring it more explicitly to recent leadership in digital transformation will increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Revise to: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel communications, CMS modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics systems that enable effective digital operations at scale. Brings deep experience in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Use “leader” instead of “professional” for a stronger senior-level tone.
- Add “governance” and “analytics” here only if you want the intro to better reflect recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap with Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination are repeated in Topline Skills and Soft Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities over tools/tasks will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and pluralize consistently: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform administration,” “Stakeholder and cross-functional coordination.”
- Replace generic or overlapping items with sharper, higher-value terms: “Digital governance,” “Content operations,” “Platform modernization,” “Audience insights and performance reporting.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Content operations & editorial workflows • Multi-channel communications • Web platform & CMS administration • Digital governance & systems architecture • Audience analytics & performance reporting • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- If targeting senior roles, lead with strategic items and move executional items later.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital strategy & transformation” and “Multi-channel communication” repeat the header and Topline Skills almost verbatim.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “Data analytics & reporting” overlap with Technical + IT and Analytics sections.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your NACo entries. Tighten it around what is new/recently distinctive—consulting impact, Drupal delivery, and the AI search initiative.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client value: “Serve as strategic communications consultant to a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, web operations, and platform improvements across enterprise communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcomes: “Redesigned workflows, analytics, and governance to improve cross-team coordination and content operations” — add metrics if possible (teams supported, sites/pages, traffic, turnaround time, adoption).
- Combine overlapping web bullets: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and member toolkits; provided front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Make the AI work a capstone bullet: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user discovery experience.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats NACo language; keep only if you can show a distinct consulting outcome.
- “Web, email, social, multimedia” is already well established elsewhere; avoid listing all channels again unless central to this role.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It would be sharper if the opening were less list-like and if each bullet emphasized outcomes, team leadership, and transformation rather than channel ownership alone.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the first sentence with a tighter leadership summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel impact more specific: add email open/click growth, social engagement/follower growth, video output, cost savings, or production volume if available.
- Tighten operations/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve executive visibility and planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial coordination/workflows” overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, analytics, and studio buildout.
- “Video as a recurring channel” is already established earlier; here, emphasize the studio and scaled in-house production capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good channel breadth, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later NACo director role and earlier producer role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing hands-on execution, editorial operations, and any concrete growth or efficiency outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social, and video, coordinating editorial delivery for advocacy, program, and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets to focus on execution and scale:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.
- Built cross-team editorial planning processes that improved coordination among communications, advocacy, and program teams.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve content consistency and delivery speed.
- If possible, add metrics: newsletter open/click rates, video cadence/views, turnaround-time improvements, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating “strengthened workflows/governance” too closely with the Director of Digital Media role.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the channel, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance

- Audience-focused content planning

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, higher-signal language:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Content governance & editorial operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider “content governance & editorial operations” instead of “editorial systems and governance” for clearer leadership emphasis.
- Use “cross-channel” rather than “multi-channel” to align with the header and sound more strategic.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-traffic, multi-publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Audience-focused content planning” is close to “Multi-channel communication” and “Editorial workflow design” elsewhere; it may be the weakest/most replaceable line.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” already appears in the header/Core Competencies, so keep it only if targeting mission-driven or association roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization

- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a raw tool list rather than a senior, impact-oriented skills statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section, so this version should emphasize higher-value capabilities and recent strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.:
- Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)
- API integrations and workflow automation
- SharePoint, Power Pages and Airtable-based systems
- AI-enabled search and content discovery
- Put Drupal/CMS modernization first, since recent roles show strongest, most credible depth there.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based systems” or “workflow systems” for cleaner phrasing.
- If space allows, add one outcome cue: “Enterprise CMS modernization for large public-facing sites” to reinforce scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and condensed.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies/Technical + IT, so avoid repeating the same wording elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack that aligns well with the most recent NACo leadership role, but it reads as a generic keyword list. Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic so it reinforces seniority rather than duplicating the Technical + IT section.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + business value, e.g. “Digital analytics, reporting & optimization.”
- Group tools and outcomes together: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI and BigQuery for KPI development, executive reporting and performance analysis.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing like “executive dashboards” or “decision-ready reporting.”
- Consider adding one strategic phrase tied to recent work: “measurement frameworks” or “insight-driven optimization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with the NACo bullet about expanding analytics infrastructure; keep this section high-level and let the work experience carry the proof.
- If space is tight, “SEO and performance analysis” may be redundant with broader “performance analysis” unless SEO is a target role keyword.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong and relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list rather than a differentiated skill cluster. Since recent roles already prove studio buildout and event/video leadership, this item should be tighter and more outcome-oriented in wording.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Video, Studio & Live Event Production”

- “Multimedia & live event production” already appears in Core Competencies, so this Topline Skills item should add specificity, not repeat the same wording
- Recent NACo experience already demonstrates studio buildout and video leadership; don’t restate those accomplishments here verbatim

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Since recent experience is strongly Drupal-led, this item should emphasize depth and recency or be tightened to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent platform first and signal level of use: “Drupal (enterprise CMS migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for scope rather than just names, e.g. “Enterprise and team-managed CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it reflects meaningful professional use; it can read as less relevant than your enterprise platform work.
- Keep formatting parallel and concise; avoid mixing platform names here with broader capabilities better covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same core platforms.
- If keeping both sections, use this one for platforms only and leave modernization/technical execution language to Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize current, implementation-level tools that support your recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Reorder by relevance/recency: JavaScript • HTML/CSS • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers unless required: use HTML/CSS instead of HTML5/CSS3
- Consider adding scope only if true: “JavaScript (front-end customization)” or “GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation)” to show applied use, not just familiarity

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “JavaScript and jQuery” plus “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills; keep one section broader and this one more tool-specific
- If Cloudflare Workers and GitHub Actions were only lightly used, remove them rather than dilute stronger, more relevant skills

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with stronger positioning already established in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a pure list to a capability-led label, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems.”
- Prioritize systems tied to recent work and higher-value automation: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana.
- Move general collaboration tools to a separate item or trim them: Slack, Teams, Basecamp, Trello are less differentiating unless central to workflow design.
- If space allows, add light context instead of only names: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana (workflow design, automation, editorial coordination).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same positioning without adding specificity.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp all signal project management; listing all four may feel redundant unless each was materially used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV. It should signal level of use and strategic application, especially since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope/strength in brief: Enterprise email campaign platforms, newsletter operations, audience engagement and member communications
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, consider ordering by strongest/recentest use rather than brand recognition

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/newsletter leadership is already covered in recent Work Experience, so avoid adding outcome claims here unless they are platform-specific
- “Engagement” may overlap with broader digital strategy language elsewhere; keep this item tool-focused, not responsibility-focused

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” production scope, and team-building contributions.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground role progression and concrete contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support day-to-day execution across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Split into 2–3 accomplishment bullets instead of one paragraph; lead with the website refresh, then multimedia production, then team/process support.
- Add measurable scope if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, publishing volume, or workflow/time-savings.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “high-impact digital content” with specifics like “livestreams, weekly video updates, and campaign content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on launching/producing the format rather than expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; frame this as early process-building support.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It would be stronger if it emphasized outcomes and framed the role as a bridge into digital/media work rather than repeating broader NACo communications themes covered in later roles.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast,” then add scope if possible (episodes, audience, internal adoption, executive/stakeholder involvement).
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: replace “coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work” with something more specific like “managed research and innovation projects for county policy and member programs.”
- Split into 2 concise accomplishment bullets, e.g.:
- Managed research and innovation projects supporting county policy initiatives and member-facing programs.
- Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production; also produced digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of projects, podcast episodes, stakeholders supported, or content produced.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital content production; later NACo roles already cover web, email, social, and video leadership in more depth.
